message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description | Notes |
|----------|---------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only element with one proton. |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average) | Weighted by natural isotopic abundance. |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among elements; drives H‑bonding. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | Energy to remove the single electron. |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72 kJ mol⁻¹) | Negative, meaning H tends to lose an electron rather than gain. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; H₂ is a gas at room temperature. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | Solidifies only at cryogenic temperatures. |
| **Density (at 25 °C)** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (0.00008988 g cm⁻³) | Lightest gas; less dense than air. |
| **Molar volume (ideal gas, 25 °C, 1 atm)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | Standard value for calculations. |
| **Molecular weight of H₂** | 2.016 g mol⁻¹ | Two hydrogen atoms per molecule. |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ | Energy to break H₂ into two H atoms. |
| **Dipole moment** | 0 D (non‑polar) | H₂ is a homonuclear diatomic molecule. |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive as a reducing agent; forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂). | Forms covalent bonds with many elements. |
| **Isotopes** | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) | ¹H ~99.98 %, ²H ~0.02 %, ³H trace. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer series in UV/visible | Classic hydrogen emission spectrum. |
| **Acid–base behavior** | Acts as a weak acid (HX → H⁺ + X⁻) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium ion. | In gas phase, H₂ is neutral. |
| **Oxidation states** | +1 (as H⁺), –1 (as H⁻) | Most common in compounds. |
| **Solubility in water** | ~0.0006 g g⁻¹ at 25 °C | Very low; hydrogen gas dissolves poorly. |
| **Flammability** | Flammable in air (range 4–75 % H₂ in air) | Explosive mixture with oxygen. |
| **Thermal conductivity** | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 25 °C) | High for a gas; good heat transfer. |
| **Specific heat capacity (gas)** | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | Low; heats up quickly. |
| **Electrical conductivity** | Very low in neutral form; high in plasma | Ionized hydrogen conducts electricity. |
| **Magnetic susceptibility** | Diamagnetic | Weakly repelled by magnetic fields. |
| **Phase diagram** | Triple point at 13.99 K, 0.00022 MPa; critical point at 33.41 K, 1.3 MPa | Shows limits of solid, liquid, gas phases. |
| **Common compounds** | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. | Forms covalent, ionic, and metallic bonds. |
| **Role in biology** | Water formation, metabolic pathways, hydrogen bonding in DNA, protein folding. | Essential for life. |
| **Industrial uses** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), ammonia synthesis (Haber process), petroleum refining, metal processing. | Key in green energy initiatives. |

---

### Quick Summary

- **Lightest element**: atomic number 1, very low density.
- **Highly reactive**: forms hydrides, acids, and fuels.
- **Low boiling/melting points**: gaseous at ambient conditions.
- **Isotopic diversity**: protium, deuterium, tritium (radioactive).
- **Key in energy & chemistry**: fuels, catalysts, solvents, biological molecules.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
